topics.topic: Status precedence when an Origin header is combined with another request-routing violation
questions: What status must be returned when a request both carries an Origin header and uses a non-POST method on MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH?
What status must be returned when a request both carries an Origin header and targets a path other than MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH?

judgement.why: This asks the same Origin-versus-method/path precedence question as P8, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether Origin validation takes precedence over method and path routing errors
quotes: Only a POST to the path equal to the imported MCP_ENDPOINT_PATH constant reaches answer_request; any other method on that path is answered 405, any other path 404, and a request carrying an Origin header 403, each without a body and without calling answer_request;
precedent.why: The Origin condition is unconditional, while 405 is limited to the correct path and every other path receives 404.

topics.topic: Whether refusal responses must read the body to recover a request id
questions: For a size or token refusal, must the body remain unread, or must it be read to recover a string or integer id?

judgement.why: This asks the same body-reading and response-id question for size or token refusals as P5, and the relevant text has not changed.

precedent.topic: Whether size/token failures must read and parse the body to preserve the request id
quotes: The body is one JSON-RPC 2.0 message, read only after the size and token checks.
The id of every response is the body's id member when the body is one JSON object whose id is a string or an integer, and null otherwise; reading it checks nothing and decides nothing.
precedent.why: The body is not read before size and token checks, so refusals at those checks cannot recover its id and use null.
